input.task: Which product on this page has the most customer reviews?

provenance: PR #34 R16, the seventh occurrence of this repo's silent-success class and the first to violate a contract that names the offending code by name: `specs/decisions/ADR-018-m31-plan-lint.md` says outright that 'a future adoption point (M32's `observe` replan) has to lint too; that is the invariant, not the two call sites', and M32's drill-down adopted its replan without one. Watched red first with the plans above: `status: success`, `verdict: PASS`, `replans: 1`, and an answer that is a LIST OF LISTS — `[["Aurora Desk Lamp", ...], ["Aurora Desk Lamp $39.00", ...]]` — offered as the answer to which product has the most reviews. Every backstop is satisfied by construction: the first plan passes the lint (exactly one `extract_all`, `rank: true`), `verifier.aggregate_needs_comparison` sees a ranked enumeration in the graded trace and is content, and the judge is never reached as a rejector because L1 passed. Proof the suite could not see it: adding the lint at that adoption point left the committed suite at 146/146 = 1.000, so no existing case reaches it at all.

triage.note: the fix is not a third hand-placed `plan_gap` call — that is how this recurred. All three places the executor rebinds `steps` now go through one nested `adopt()` that lints and splices together, so a fourth adoption point cannot be added without one. Asserted structurally per PR #34 R13: `trace_actions` pins that the run got as far as the `observe` and stopped there, and `replans: 0` that the refused plan was never counted as progress — a reason-string assertion would pass on any of the drill-down's four refusal exits.
